test.title: Part 1–4: Cambridge IELTS 19 Academic Listening Test 2

items.quote: He's called a 'coordinator' — his name's Gary Mathieson.
items.prompt: Coordinator: Gary ____

explanation.en: The coordinator is Gary Mathieson, subsequently spelled M-A-T-H-I-E-S-O-N; use the surname only.
explanation.kk: Үйлестіруші — Гари Mathieson; тегі кейін M-A-T-H-I-E-S-O-N деп айтылады. Тек тегін жазыңыз.
explanation.ru: Координатор — Гэри Mathieson; фамилию затем диктуют M-A-T-H-I-E-S-O-N. Нужна только фамилия.

items.quote: When I first spoke to Gary on the phone, he said it was a class for beginners, but I was still worried that everyone would be better than me, but we were all equally hopeless!
items.prompt: Level: ____

explanation.en: Gary describes the group as a class for beginners; knowing a few chords does not make it an advanced class.
explanation.kk: Гари топты beginners сыныбы дейді; бірнеше аккорд білу жоғары деңгейді білдірмейді.
explanation.ru: Гэри называет группу классом для начинающих, beginners; знание нескольких аккордов не означает продвинутый уровень.

items.quote: Well, when I joined the group, they were meeting in Gary's home, but as the group got bigger, he decided to book a room at the college in town.
items.prompt: Place: the ____

explanation.en: The group now meets at the college; Gary’s home was its previous venue.
explanation.kk: Топ қазір college ғимаратында жиналады; Гаридің үйі — бұрынғы орын.
explanation.ru: Теперь группа собирается в колледже, college; дом Гэри — прежнее место.

items.quote: It's just beyond there at the bottom of New Street near the city roundabout.
items.prompt: Place: ____ Street; first floor, Room T347

explanation.en: Coleman corrects the guessed Lock Street to New Street; “Street” is already printed after the gap.
explanation.kk: Колман Lock Street деген болжамды New Street деп түзетеді; Street бос орыннан кейін берілген.
explanation.ru: Колман исправляет догадку Lock Street на New Street; Street уже дано после пропуска.

items.quote: It used to be 10.30 and that suited me well, but now we meet at 11.
items.prompt: Time: Thursday morning at ____

explanation.en: The meeting time changed from 10.30 to 11; the question asks for the current time.
explanation.kk: Уақыт 10.30-дан 11-ге өзгерген; қазіргі уақытты жазыңыз.
explanation.ru: Время изменилось с 10.30 на 11; нужно нынешнее время.

items.quote: There's a website called 'The perfect instrument' that sells all kinds of guitars, violins and so on.
items.prompt: Recommended website: ‘The perfect ____’

explanation.en: The website is called “The perfect instrument”; guitars and violins are examples of what it sells.
explanation.kk: Сайттың атауы — The perfect instrument; гитара мен скрипка — атау емес, сатылатын заттар.
explanation.ru: Сайт называется The perfect instrument; гитары и скрипки — товары, а не название.

groups.title: Guitar Group
groups.instruction: Complete the form below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.quote: Some people have an app they use, but others do it by ear.
items.prompt: Tuning guitars: using an app or by ____

explanation.en: Some learners tune with an app, while others do it by ear; the app is already supplied in the table.
explanation.kk: Біреулер қосымшамен, өзгелері by ear арқылы баптайды; қосымша кестеде берілген.
explanation.ru: Одни настраивают через приложение, другие на слух, by ear; приложение уже указано в таблице.

items.quote: Sometimes we all just start laughing because we're so bad at keeping time, so Gary starts clapping to help us.
items.prompt: Strumming chords: keeping time while the teacher is ____

explanation.en: Gary starts clapping to help learners keep time; strumming is the learners’ activity.
explanation.kk: Гари ырғақты ұстауға көмектесу үшін clapping жасайды; ішекті қағу — оқушылар әрекеті.
explanation.ru: Гэри хлопает, clapping, чтобы помочь соблюдать ритм; по струнам играют ученики.

items.quote: He often brings a recording of the song and plays it to us first.
items.prompt: Playing songs: often listening to a ____ of a song

explanation.en: Gary brings a recording and plays it before the learners practise the song.
explanation.kk: Гари recording әкеліп, әнді жаттықтыру алдында ойнатады.
explanation.ru: Гэри приносит запись, recording, и включает её до разучивания песни.

items.quote: The only trouble is that he sometimes gets us to play one at a time — you know, alone.
items.prompt: Playing single notes and simple tunes: playing together, then ____

explanation.en: Playing “one at a time” is immediately explained as playing alone.
explanation.kk: One at a time, яғни кезекпен жеке ойнау, бірден alone деп түсіндіріледі.
explanation.ru: Игра по одному, one at a time, сразу поясняется словом alone.

Activity
Notes

groups.title: A typical 45-minute guitar lesson
groups.instruction: Complete the table below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

parts.context: Two friends discuss joining a guitar group and a typical lesson.

transcript.text: Hi Coleman, how are you?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Good, thanks.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: I wanted to have a chat with you because our friend Josh told me that you've joined a guitar group and it sounds interesting.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: I'd really like to learn myself.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Why don't you come along?
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: I'm sure there's room for another person.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Really?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: So — who runs the classes?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: He's called a 'coordinator' — his name's Gary Mathieson.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Let me note that down.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Gary....
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: How do you spell his surname?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: It's M-A-T-H-I-E-S-O-N.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Right, thanks.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: He's retired, actually, but he's a really nice guy and he used to play in a lot of bands.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Thanks.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: So how long have you been going?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: About a month now.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: And could you play anything before you started?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: I knew a few chords, but that's all.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: I'm sure everyone will be better than me.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: That's what I thought, too.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: When I first spoke to Gary on the phone, he said it was a class for beginners, but I was still worried that everyone would be better than me, but we were all equally hopeless!
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Oh, that's reassuring.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: So where do you meet?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Well, when I joined the group, they were meeting in Gary's home, but as the group got bigger, he decided to book a room at the college in town.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: I prefer going there.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: I know that place.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: I used to go to tap dancing classes there when I was at secondary school.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: I haven't been since, though and I can't remember what road it's in . is it Lock Street?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: It's just beyond there at the bottom of New Street near the city roundabout.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Yes, of course.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: The guitar club is on the first floor in Room T 347.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: And when do you meet?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Is it at the weekend?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: We meet on Thursdays.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: It used to be 10.30 and that suited me well, but now we meet at 11.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: The class that's in there before us asked if they could have the room for another 30 minutes.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Oh, I see.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Well, I'd love to come, but I don't have a guitar.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Well, you can always buy a second-hand one.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: There's a website called 'The perfect instrument' that sells all kinds of guitars, violins and so on.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: I'm sure you'll find something there.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: So what's a typical lesson like with Gary?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Well, he always starts by getting us to tune our guitars.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: That takes about five minutes.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Uhuh.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Some people have an app they use, but others do it by ear.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Gary goes round and helps them.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: And while he's doing that, he tells us what he's going to do during the lesson.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: First, we usually spend about ten minutes doing some strumming.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: So is that using ... what are they called . plectrums?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: No — we just use our thumbs.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Much easier.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Gary reminds us where to put our fingers for each chord and then we play them together.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Sometimes we all just start laughing because we're so bad at keeping time, so Gary starts clapping to help us.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Do you learn to play any songs?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Yes — we do at least one song with words and chords.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: I mean that's harder than you think.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Oh, I'm sure it is!
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: That part of the lesson takes about 15 minutes.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: He often brings a recording of the song and plays it to us first.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Then he hands out the song and if there's a new chord in it, we practise that before we play it together — but really slowly.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Do you do any finger picking?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: That's the last ten minutes of the lesson, when we pick out the individual notes from a tune he's made up.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: It's always quite simple.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: That must be hard, though.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: It is, but people like it because they can really concentrate and if we're all playing well, it sounds quite impressive.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: The only trouble is that he sometimes gets us to play one at a time — you know, alone.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: That's scary.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: It is, but I've got used to it now.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: At the end he spends about five minutes telling us what to practise for the following week.
transcript.speaker: COLEMAN

transcript.text: Well, thanks Coleman.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: I'll go and have a look at that website, I think.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

items.quote: I'd been really keen on boats as a teenager, and I thought if I went to live by the sea, I might be able to pursue that interest a bit more in my free time.
items.prompt: What made David leave London and move to Northsea?

options.text: He was eager to develop a hobby.
He wanted to work shorter hours.
He found his job in website design unsatisfying.

explanation.en: He wanted to pursue boating; his job was interesting and shorter hours are not given as the reason.
explanation.kk: Ол қайыққа қызығушылығын дамытқысы келді; жұмысы қызықты болды, уақыт қысқарту себеп емес.
explanation.ru: Он хотел заниматься лодками; работа была интересной, сокращение часов не названо причиной.

items.quote: It was built 15 years ago with funds provided by a generous member of the public who'd lived here all her life.
items.prompt: The Lifeboat Institution in Northsea was built with money provided by

options.text: a local organisation.
a local resident.
the local council.

explanation.en: A woman who had lived there all her life donated the funds, rather than the council or an organisation.
explanation.kk: Қаржыны осында өмір бойы тұрған әйел берді; кеңес не ұйым емес.
explanation.ru: Средства дала женщина, всю жизнь жившая здесь, а не совет или организация.

items.quote: They gave me tests for colour blindness and they thought I might have a problem there, but it turned out I was OK.
items.prompt: In his health assessment, the doctor was concerned about the fact that David

options.text: might be colour blind.
was rather short-sighted.
had undergone eye surgery.

explanation.en: Colour blindness was suspected; his short-sightedness had already been corrected by surgery.
explanation.kk: Түс ажырата алмауы мүмкін деп ойлады; алыстан көрмеуі операциямен түзетілген.
explanation.ru: Подозревали дальтонизм; близорукость уже исправили операцией.

items.quote: Our target's to get there in five minutes, then we try to get the boat off the dock and out to sea in another six to eight minutes.
items.prompt: After arriving at the lifeboat station, they aim to launch the boat within

options.text: five minutes.
six to eight minutes.
eight and a half minutes.

explanation.en: Launch takes another six to eight minutes after arrival; five minutes is travel and eight and a half is the national average.
explanation.kk: Келгеннен кейін тағы 6–8 минут керек; бес минут — станцияға жету, 8,5 — елдік орташа көрсеткіш.
explanation.ru: После прибытия нужно ещё 6–8 минут; пять минут — дорога к станции, 8,5 — среднее по стране.

items.quote: And it's ultimately my decision whether it's safe to launch the boat.
items.prompt: As a ‘helmsman’, David has the responsibility of deciding

options.text: who will be the members of his crew.
what equipment it will be necessary to take.
if the lifeboat should be launched.

explanation.en: He decides whether launching is safe; he checks equipment rather than selecting what to take.
explanation.kk: Ол қайықты түсіру қауіпсіз бе деп шешеді; жабдықты таңдамай, тексереді.
explanation.ru: Именно он решает, безопасно ли спускать лодку; оборудование он проверяет, а не выбирает.

items.quote: A lot of people underestimate how quickly conditions can change at sea, so I speak to youth groups and sailing clubs in the area about the sorts of problems that sailors and swimmers can have if the weather suddenly gets bad.
items.prompt: As well as going out on the lifeboat, David

options.text: gives talks on safety at sea.
helps with fundraising.
recruits new volunteers.

explanation.en: He gives safety talks to youth groups and sailing clubs; other volunteers organise fundraising.
explanation.kk: Ол жастар мен желкен клубтарына қауіпсіздік туралы айтады; қаражатты басқа еріктілер жинайды.
explanation.ru: Он выступает перед молодёжью и яхт-клубами о безопасности; средства собирают другие добровольцы.

groups.title: Working as a lifeboat volunteer
groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.quote: The training we get is a continuous process, focusing on technical competence and safe handling techniques, and it's given me the confidence to deal with extreme situations without panicking.
items.prompt: Which TWO things does David say about the lifeboat volunteer training?

options.text: The residential course developed his leadership skills.
The training in use of ropes and knots was quite brief.
The training exercises have built up his mental strength.
The casualty care activities were particularly challenging for him.
The wave tank activities provided practice in survival techniques.

explanation.en: Training built mental strength and the wave tank practised survival. Knots received extensive training and first aid was already familiar.
explanation.kk: Дайындық сабыр сақтауды үйретті, толқын бассейні аман қалуға жаттықтырды. Түйінге көп уақыт бөлінді; алғашқы көмек бұрыннан таныс еді.
explanation.ru: Подготовка укрепила самообладание, а бассейн с волнами учил выживанию. Узлам уделяли много времени; первая помощь уже была знакома.

items.quote: They're a great group — we're like a family really, which helps when you're dragging yourself out of bed on a cold stormy night.
items.prompt: Which TWO things does David find most motivating about the work he does?

options.text: working as part of a team
experiences when working in winter
being thanked by those he has helped
the fact that it keeps him fit
the chance to develop new equipment

explanation.en: The close team and rewarding winter rescues motivate him; thanks, fitness and equipment development are not stated as motives.
explanation.kk: Оны тату команда мен күрделі қысқы құтқарулар ынталандырады; алғыс, дене шынықтыру, жабдық жасау аталмады.
explanation.ru: Его мотивируют дружная команда и серьёзные зимние спасения; благодарность, фитнес и разработка оборудования не названы.

parts.context: David describes his work and training as a lifeboat volunteer.

transcript.text: I never really planned to be a lifeboat volunteer when I came to live in Northsea.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: I'd been working in London as a website designer, but although that was interesting, I didn't like city life.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: I'd been really keen on boats as a teenager, and I thought if I went to live by the sea, I might be able to pursue that interest a bit more in my free time.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: Then I found that the Lifeboat Institution was looking for volunteers, so I decided to apply.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: The Lifeboat Institution building here in Northsea's hard to miss, it's one of the largest in the country.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: It was built 15 years ago with funds provided by a generous member of the public who'd lived here all her life.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: As the Lifeboat Institution is a charity that relies on that kind of donation, rather than funding provided by the government, that was a huge help to us.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: When I applied, I had to have a health assessment.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: The doctors were particularly interested in my vision.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: I used to be short-sighted, so I'd had to wear glasses, but I'd had laser eye surgery two years earlier so that was OK.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: They gave me tests for colour blindness and they thought I might have a problem there, but it turned out I was OK.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: When the coastguard gets an alert, all the volunteers are contacted and rush to the lifeboat station.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: Our target's to get there in five minutes, then we try to get the boat off the dock and out to sea in another six to eight minutes.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: Our team's proud that we usually achieve that — the average time across the country's eight and a half minutes.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: I've recently qualified as what's called a 'helmsman', which means I have the ultimate responsibility for the lifeboat.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: I have to check that the equipment we use is in working order — the crew have special life jackets that can support up to four people in the water.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: And it's ultimately my decision whether it's safe to launch the boat.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: But it's very rare not to launch it, even in the worst weather.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: As well as going out on the lifeboat, my work involves other things too.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: A lot of people underestimate how quickly conditions can change at sea, so I speak to youth groups and sailing clubs in the area about the sorts of problems that sailors and swimmers can have if the weather suddenly gets bad.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: We also have a lot of volunteers who organise activities to raise money for us, and we couldn't manage without them.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: The training we get is a continuous process, focusing on technical competence and safe handling techniques, and it's given me the confidence to deal with extreme situations without panicking.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: I was glad I'd done a first aid course before I started, as that's a big help with the casualty care activities we do.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: We've done a lot on how to deal with ropes and tie knots — that's an essential skill.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: After a year, I did a one-week residential course, led by specialists.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: They had a wave-tank where they could create extreme weather conditions — so we could get experience at what to do if the boat turned over in a storm at night, for example.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: Since I started, I've had to deal with a range of emergency situations.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: But the work's hugely motivating.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: It's not just about saving lives — I've learned a lot about the technology involved.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: My background in IT's been useful here, and I can use my expertise to help other volunteers.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: They're a great group — we're like a family really, which helps when you're dragging yourself out of bed on a cold stormy night.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: But actually, it's the colder months that can be the most rewarding time.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: That's when the incidents tend to be more serious, and you realise that you can make a huge difference to the outcome.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

transcript.text: So if any of you listeners are interested.
transcript.speaker: DAVID

items.quote: Well, before I started reading it, I thought recycling footwear, well, although it's quite interesting, perhaps there isn't enough to say about it, cos we put shoes in recycling bins, they go to charity shops and that's about it.
items.prompt: At first, Don thought the topic of recycling footwear might be too

options.text: limited in scope.
hard to research.
boring for listeners.

explanation.en: Don thought there was not enough to say; lack of interest or research difficulty was not his concern.
explanation.kk: Дон айтуға материал аз деп ойлады; қызықсыздық не зерттеу қиындығы мәселе емес.
explanation.ru: Дон думал, что нечего подробно рассказать; интерес и сложность исследования не проблема.

items.quote: Actually, I think some of them look quite smart on pupils . . better than a scruffy old pair of shoes.
items.prompt: When discussing trainers, Bella and Don disagree about

options.text: how popular they are among young people.
how suitable they are for school.
how quickly they wear out.

explanation.en: Don thinks trainers are too casual for school; Bella thinks some look smart on pupils.
explanation.kk: Дон кроссовканы мектепке тым қарапайым дейді; Белла кейбірін жарасымды санайды.
explanation.ru: Дон считает кроссовки слишком повседневными для школы; Белла считает некоторые нарядными.

items.quote: I must admit, I've recycled some perfectly good shoes, that haven't gone out of fashion and still fit, just because they don't look great on me any more.
items.prompt: Bella says that she sometimes recycles shoes because

options.text: they no longer fit.
she no longer likes them.
they are no longer in fashion.

explanation.en: The shoes still fit and are in fashion, but she no longer likes how they look on her.
explanation.kk: Аяқкиім шақ әрі сәннен шықпаған, бірақ оған сыртқы түрі ұнамайды.
explanation.ru: Туфли подходят и не вышли из моды, но ей больше не нравится их вид.

items.quote: But then it said that the amount of recycled footwear has fallen: it's 6 percent now compared to a previous level of 11 percent.
items.prompt: What did the article say that confused Don?

options.text: Public consumption of footwear has risen.
Less footwear is recycled now than in the past.
People dispose of more footwear than they used to.

explanation.en: He was confused by recycling falling from 11 to 6 percent despite increased sales.
explanation.kk: Сатылым өскенде қайта өңдеу 11-ден 6 пайызға түскені таңғалдырды.
explanation.ru: Удивило падение переработки с 11 до 6 процентов, несмотря на рост продаж.

groups.title: Recycling footwear
groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.quote: He said they were probably expensive — the material was suede and they were beige in colour — it looked like someone had only worn them once, but in a very wet field so the heels were too stained with mud and grass to re-sell them.
items.prompt: the high-heeled shoes

explanation.en: Mud and grass stained the heels; price and material were not reasons for rejection.
explanation.kk: Өкшелер балшық пен шөпке былғанған; бағасы мен материалы себеп емес.
explanation.ru: Каблуки испачканы грязью и травой; цена и материал не причина отказа.

items.quote: One of the shoes was a much lighter shade than the other one — it had obviously been left in the sun.
items.prompt: the ankle boots

explanation.en: One boot faded in the sun; worn heels were explicitly not the problem.
explanation.kk: Бір етік күнге оңған; тозған өкше мәселе болған жоқ.
explanation.ru: Один ботинок выцвел на солнце; изношенные каблуки не были проблемой.

items.quote: You'd think it would have been easy to find the other, but it wasn't.
items.prompt: the baby shoes

explanation.en: The other shoe could not be found; being new was not itself a reason for rejection.
explanation.kk: Екінші аяқкиім табылмады; жаңа болғаны бас тарту себебі емес.
explanation.ru: Не нашли второй туфель; новизна сама по себе не причина отказа.

items.quote: One of the soles was so worn under the foot that you could put your finger through it.
items.prompt: the trainers

explanation.en: A sole was worn through, leaving a hole; it was not split stitching.
explanation.kk: Табаны тесілгенше тозған; тігістің сөгілуі емес.
explanation.ru: Подошва протёрлась до дырки; речь не о разошедшемся шве.

groups.title: Rejected footwear

options.text: one shoe was missing
the colour of one shoe had faded
one shoe had a hole in it
the shoes were brand new
the shoes were too dirty
the stitching on the shoes was broken

groups.instruction: What reasons did the recycling manager give for rejecting footwear, according to the students? Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to the questions.

items.quote: It was because the pairs of shoes weren't identical.
items.prompt: Why did the project to make ‘new’ shoes out of old shoes fail?

options.text: People believed the ‘new’ pairs of shoes were unhygienic.
There were not enough good parts to use in the old shoes.
The shoes in the ‘new’ pairs were not completely alike.

explanation.en: The shoes in each pair were not identical; the hygiene explanation is explicitly rejected.
explanation.kk: Жұптар бірдей болмады; микроб туралы болжам тікелей жоққа шығарылды.
explanation.ru: Пары не совпадали внешне; предположение о микробах прямо отвергнуто.

items.quote: It's not as simple as you first think, and we can show that by taking a very different approach to it.

with relevant images.
in a straightforward way.

explanation.ru: Они предлагают иной подход и общую картину; простота и изображения не их вывод.

parts.context: Two students plan a presentation on recycling footwear.

transcript.text: Hi Don — did you get the copy of the article on recycling footwear that I emailed you?
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: Yeah — it's here .
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: I've had a look at it.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: So do you think it's a good topic for our presentation?
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: Well, before I started reading it, I thought recycling footwear, well, although it's quite interesting, perhaps there isn't enough to say about it, cos we put shoes in recycling bins, they go to charity shops and that's about it.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: . but there's much more to it than that.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: I realise that now and I'm keen to research the topic more.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: That's great.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: One of the things I didn't realise until I read the article was just how many pairs of trainers get recycled!
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: Well, a lot of young people wear them all the time now.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: They've become more popular than ordinary shoes.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: I know.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: I guess they are very hard-wearing, but don't they look a bit casual for school uniform?
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: I don't think they're right for that.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: Actually, I think some of them look quite smart on pupils . . better than a scruffy old pair of shoes.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: So do you keep shoes a long time?
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: Yes.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: Though I do tend to wear my old pairs for doing dirty jobs like cleaning my bike.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: I must admit, I've recycled some perfectly good shoes, that haven't gone out of fashion and still fit, just because they don't look great on me any more.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: That's awful isn't it?
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: I think it's common because there's so much choice.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: The article did say that recent sales of footwear have increased enormously.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: That didn't surprise me.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: No.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: But then it said that the amount of recycled footwear has fallen: it's 6 percent now compared to a previous level of 11 percent.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: That doesn't seem to make sense.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: That's because not everything goes through the recycling process.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: Some footwear just isn't good enough to re-sell, for one reason or another, and gets rejected.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: So let's find some examples in the article of footwear that was rejected for recycling.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: OK.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: Mmm.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: Let's start with the ladies' high-heeled shoes.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: What did he say about those?
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: He said they were probably expensive — the material was suede and they were beige in colour — it looked like someone had only worn them once, but in a very wet field so the heels were too stained with mud and grass to re-sell them.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: OK ... and the leather ankle boots.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: What was wrong with them?
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: Apparently, the heels were worn — but that wasn't the problem.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: One of the shoes was a much lighter shade than the other one — it had obviously been left in the sun.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: Sure.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: Then there were the red baby shoes.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: Oh yes — we're told to tie shoes together when we put them in a recycling bin, but people often don't bother.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.text: You'd think it would have been easy to find the other, but it wasn't.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: That was a shame because they were obviously new.
transcript.speaker: BELLA

transcript.text: The trainers were interesting.
transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.speaker: DON

transcript.speaker: DON

items.quote: They are also sometimes called 'water bears': 'water' because that's where they thrive best, and 'bear' because of the way they move. 'Moss piglet' is another name for tardigrades because of the way they look when viewed from the front.
items.prompt: Also known as water ‘bears’ (due to how they ____) and ‘moss piglets’

explanation.en: They are called water bears because of the way they move; appearance explains the separate name “moss piglet”.
explanation.kk: Water bears атауы олардың move қозғалысына байланысты; сыртқы түрі басқа moss piglet атауын түсіндіреді.
explanation.ru: Название water bears объясняется тем, как они двигаются, move; внешность объясняет другое название, moss piglet.

items.quote: They have a body which is short, and also rounded — a bit like a barrel — and the body comprises four segments.
items.prompt: A ____ round body and four pairs of legs

explanation.en: The body is described as short and rounded; “round” is already supplied in the notes.
explanation.kk: Дене short және домалақ деп сипатталған; round жазбада берілген.
explanation.ru: Тело названо коротким, short, и округлым; round уже дано в заметках.

items.quote: I should also say that some species don't have any claws; what they have are discs, and these work by means of suction.
items.prompt: Claws or ____ for gripping

explanation.en: Some species have suction discs instead of claws; both enable gripping.
explanation.kk: Кейбір түрінде тырнақ орнына discs сорғыштары бар; екеуі де жабысуға көмектеседі.
explanation.ru: У некоторых видов вместо когтей присоски, discs; обе структуры помогают цепляться.

items.quote: Instead, oxygen and also blood are transported in a fluid that fills the cavity of the body.
items.prompt: Body filled with a liquid that carries both ____ and blood

explanation.en: A fluid in the body carries oxygen and blood; lungs and other respiratory organs are absent.
explanation.kk: Денедегі сұйықтық oxygen мен қанды тасиды; өкпе және тыныс алу мүшелері жоқ.
explanation.ru: Жидкость в теле переносит кислород, oxygen, и кровь; лёгких и дыхательных органов нет.

items.quote: The tardigrade's mouth is a kind of tube that can open outwards to reveal teeth-like structures known as 'stylets'.
items.prompt: Mouth shaped like a ____ with teeth called stylets

explanation.en: The mouth is described as a tube; the teeth-like structures are called stylets.
explanation.kk: Ауыз tube ретінде сипатталған; stylets — тіске ұқсас құрылымдардың атауы.
explanation.ru: Рот напоминает трубку, tube; stylets — название зубоподобных структур.

groups.title: Tardigrades — name and physical appearance
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.quote: There's been some interesting research which has found that tardigrades are capable of surviving radiation and very high pressure, and they're also able to withstand temperatures as cold as —200 degrees centigrade, or highs of more than 148 degrees centigrade, which is incredibly hot.
items.prompt: Very resilient and can exist in very low or high ____

explanation.en: They withstand very low and high temperatures; the gap asks for the physical condition, not a numerical value.
explanation.kk: Олар төмен және жоғары temperatures жағдайына шыдайды; сан емес, жағдай түрі сұралады.
explanation.ru: Они выдерживают низкие и высокие температуры, temperatures; нужен вид условия, а не число.

items.quote: While in a state of cryptobiosis, tardigrades produce a protein that protects their DNA.
items.prompt: A type of ____ ensures their DNA is not damaged.

explanation.en: During cryptobiosis they produce a protein that protects their DNA; “tun” names their curled state.
explanation.kk: Криптобиозда ДНҚ қорғайтын protein түзіледі; tun — жиырылған күйінің атауы.
explanation.ru: При криптобиозе вырабатывается белок, protein, защищающий ДНК; tun — название свёрнутого состояния.

items.quote: There are currently several tests taking place in space, to determine how long tardigrades might be able to survive there.
items.prompt: Research is underway to find out how many days they can stay alive in ____.

explanation.en: Current tests take place in space to measure survival time; 10 days is the reported record, not the location.
explanation.kk: Қазіргі сынақ space ішінде өтеді; он күн — орын емес, рекорд.
explanation.ru: Нынешние испытания идут в космосе, space; десять дней — рекорд, а не место.

items.quote: They suck the juices from moss, or extract fluid from seaweed, but some species prey on other tardigrades, from other species or within their own.
items.prompt: Consume liquids, e.g., those found in moss or ____

explanation.en: They extract fluid from seaweed as well as moss; the notes already provide moss.
explanation.kk: Олар seaweed пен мүктен сұйықтық алады; мүк жазбада берілген.
explanation.ru: Они извлекают жидкость из водорослей, seaweed, и мха; мох уже указан.

items.quote: So, it will probably come as no surprise to you, that tardigrades have not been evaluated by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and are not on any endangered list.
items.prompt: They are not considered to be ____.

explanation.en: They are not on any endangered list; their long survival history supports this classification.
explanation.kk: Олар endangered тізімінде жоқ; ұзақ уақыт тіршілік етуі осы мәртебені қолдайды.
explanation.ru: Их нет в списках endangered; длительная история выживания подтверждает этот статус.

groups.title: Tardigrades — habitat, cryptobiosis, feeding and conservation
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

parts.context: A student presents research on tardigrades.

transcript.text: For my project on invertebrates, I chose to study tardigrades.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: These are microscopic — or to be more precise — near-microscopic animals.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There are well over a thousand known species of these tiny animals, which belong to the phylum Tardigrada.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Most tardigrades range in length from 0.05 to 1 millimetre, though the largest species can grow to be 1.2 millimetres in length.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They are also sometimes called 'water bears': 'water' because that's where they thrive best, and 'bear' because of the way they move. 'Moss piglet' is another name for tardigrades because of the way they look when viewed from the front.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They were first discovered in Germany in 1773 by Johann Goeze, who coined the name Tardigrada.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: As I say, there are many different species of tardigrade — too many to describe here — but, generally speaking, the different species share similar physical traits.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They have a body which is short, and also rounded — a bit like a barrel — and the body comprises four segments.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Each segment has a pair of legs, at the end of which are between four and eight sharp claws.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: I should also say that some species don't have any claws; what they have are discs, and these work by means of suction.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They enable the tardigrade to cling on to surfaces or to grip its prey.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Within the body, there are no lungs, or any organs for breathing at all.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Instead, oxygen and also blood are transported in a fluid that fills the cavity of the body.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: As far as the tardigrade's head is concerned, the best way I can describe this is that it looks rather strange — a bit squashed even — though many of the websites I looked at described its appearance as cute, which isn't exactly very scientific.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The tardigrade's mouth is a kind of tube that can open outwards to reveal teeth-like structures known as 'stylets'.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: These are sharp enough to pierce plant or animal cells.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: So, where are tardigrades found?
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Well, they live in every part of the world, in a variety of habitats: most commonly, on the bed of a lake, or on many kinds of plants or in very wet environments.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There's been some interesting research which has found that tardigrades are capable of surviving radiation and very high pressure, and they're also able to withstand temperatures as cold as —200 degrees centigrade, or highs of more than 148 degrees centigrade, which is incredibly hot.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: It has been said that tardigrades could survive long after human beings have been wiped out, even in the event of an asteroid hitting the earth.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: If conditions become too extreme and tardigrades are at risk of drying out, they enter a state called cryptobiosis.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They curl into a ball, called a tun — that's T-U-N — by retracting their head and legs, and their metabolism drops to less than one percent of normal levels.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They can remain like this until they are re-introduced to water, when they will come back to life in a matter of a few hours.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: While in a state of cryptobiosis, tardigrades produce a protein that protects their DNA.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: In 2016, scientists revived two tardigrades that had been tuns for more than 30 years.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There was a report that, in 1948, a 120-year-old tun was revived, but this experiment has never been repeated.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: There are currently several tests taking place in space, to determine how long tardigrades might be able to survive there.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: I believe the record so far is 10 days.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: So, erm, moving on.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: In terms of their diet, tardigrades consume liquids in order to survive.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Although they have teeth, they don't use these for chewing.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They suck the juices from moss, or extract fluid from seaweed, but some species prey on other tardigrades, from other species or within their own.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: I suppose this isn't surprising, given that tardigrades are mainly comprised of liquid and are coated with a type of gel.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Finally, I'd like to mention the conservation status of tardigrades.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: It is estimated that they have been in existence for approximately half a billion years and, in that time, they have survived five mass extinctions.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: So, it will probably come as no surprise to you, that tardigrades have not been evaluated by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and are not on any endangered list.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Some researchers have described them as thriving.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Does anyone have any questions they'd like to ask?
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER
